bib.title: It's Not Just Size That Matters: Small Language Models Are Also Few-Shot Learners

question: Can small masked language models, trained with pattern-exploiting training (PET) on 32 labelled examples, match GPT-3 priming on SuperGLUE?
hypothesis: Cloze-question reformulation with gradient-based finetuning lets a model with orders of magnitude fewer parameters reach GPT-3-level few-shot performance.
contributions: Generalise PET to verbalizers of multiple tokens (COPA, WSC, ReCoRD) with max-first decoding and a hinge loss
Show ALBERT with PET/iPET beats GPT-3 on SuperGLUE with 32 examples using 0.1% of the parameters
Release FewGLUE (32 labelled + up to 20,000 unlabelled examples per task) and analyse factors: patterns, unlabeled data, labeled data use, model type, multi-mask decoding, example choice

method.summary: ALBERT-xxlarge-v2 is finetuned as a masked LM on cloze-formatted inputs (pattern-verbalizer pairs), several patterns are ensembled and distilled into a sequence classifier using unlabeled data; iPET repeats this over generations. Compared to GPT-3 primed with 32 examples on SuperGLUE.

datasets.name: FewGLUE (SuperGLUE subset)
datasets.size: 32 labelled examples per task (32 questions for MultiRC and ReCoRD; positives only for WSC)
datasets.split: first 32 of the training set shuffled with a fixed random seed
datasets.preprocessing: none except truncating to max sequence length (longest-first), before patterns applied

datasets.name: FewGLUE unlabeled
datasets.size: up to 20,000 unlabeled examples per task (BoolQ 9,427; CB 20,000; COPA 400; MultiRC 5,100; ReCoRD 20,000; RTE 20,000; WiC 6,000; WSC 554)
datasets.split: training-set labels removed; CB and RTE topped up from MNLI training set

datasets.name: SuperGLUE dev/test
datasets.size: dev: BoolQ 3,270; CB 57; COPA 100; MultiRC 953; ReCoRD 10,000; RTE 278; WiC 638; WSC 104. test: BoolQ 3,245; CB 250; COPA 500; MultiRC 1,800; ReCoRD 10,000; RTE 300; WiC 1,400; WSC 146

other.note: numbers taken from Brown et al. (2020); authors had no API access

training.objective: PET: cross entropy on pattern-verbalizer MLM, multi-mask tasks use multi-class hinge loss (margin 1 in log prob); distillation: cross entropy to soft labels
training.steps: pet_max_steps 250 per PET model; sc_max_steps 5,000 for final classifier
training.compute: 250-step PET model about 45 minutes; labeling unlabeled 0.2-1.5 hours per model; final classifier 5,000 steps about 2.5 hours on average
training.wall_clock: several hours on a single GPU
training.seeds: 3 models per pattern; fixed seed s0 for FewGLUE sampling

inference.decoding: max-first autoregressive filling of masks for multi-token verbalizers; greedy for WSC with one mask
inference.samples: Fig 4 averages over three training runs
inference.prompting: cloze patterns with verbalizers (see prompts); GPT-3 baseline primed with 32 examples

eval.protocol: no dev set used for hyperparameters; same hyperparameters as Schick and Schütze (2021); single fixed training set except Section 5.6

prompts.text: p. Question: q? Answer: __. | p. Based on the previous passage, q? __. | Based on the following passage, q? __. p
s The pronoun '*p*' refers to __. | s In the previous sentence, the pronoun '*p*' refers to __. | s In the passage above, what does the pronoun '*p*' refer to? Answer: __.
p. Question: q? Is it a? __. | p. Question: q? Is the correct answer "a"? __. | p. Based on the previous passage, q? Is "a" a correct answer? __.

limits: GPT-3 not available to authors; analysis only on PET
Comparison with GPT-3 not on identical examples (GPT-3 uses different examples per test example; its training sets were not available)
PET needs unlabeled data (up to 20,000 per task) and hand-written patterns where GPT-3 used one
Still clearly below SotA trained on full SuperGLUE (89.3 avg)
ALBERT crucial: other LMs perform worse; GPT-2 differs in several factors, unidirectionality not isolated
Large variance across training example sets
Only classification; generative tasks left to future work
Priming with XLNet could not be run on MultiRC (more than 10,000 tokens)

terms.definition: GPT-3 is given a few demonstrations of inputs and corresponding outputs as context for its predictions, but no gradient updates are performed.
pattern-verbalizer pair: a pattern mapping inputs to cloze questions with a single mask and a verbalizer mapping outputs to tokens
